evidence.quote: We propose a $35 million class fund distributed automatically, plus a separately stated $7 million fee-and-expense request subject to court approval.

The $5 million fee request covers invested time and expenses, remains subject to court approval, and any reduction benefits the class. Accepting now avoids unnecessary litigation and competing-settlement risk.

summary: Hargrove raised fees alongside class relief in its opening offer, before the class fund was settled. Whitcombe’s private reasoning considered whether the fee request covered its invested time and expenses when deciding to accept. The record does not show a fee-for-fund trade, defense use of fees to reduce class relief, or a misleading declaration.
